analysis: The PR adds an admin-only per-machine Autopilot API. Routes are in coordinator/api/routes.go, hunk @@ -288: GET /v1/admin/autopilot/machines and PATCH /v1/admin/autopilot/machines/{machine_id}. Both are wrapped in s.access.RequireAuth and routed to handleAdminAutopilotMachines (autopilot_handlers.go:26-32), which sets Cache-Control: no-store and then calls IsAdminAuthorized before the new autopilotapi.MachineHandler. This matches the existing admin Autopilot handlers (TB-006, T-004, T-024). The handler in coordinator/api/autopilot/machines.go follows the controls expected for an admin mutation. PATCH bodies are capped at 1024 bytes with MaxBytesReader. The body is parsed token by token, so only a single case-sensitive desired_mode key is accepted, duplicates and trailing data are rejected, and the value must be shadow or live. machine_id and the after cursor must be canonical lowercase nonzero UUIDs. limit is bounded to 1-200. Both operations run under a 2s timeout. Errors are generic and do not leak internals. Authorization is applied before any controller call, so no unauthenticated or consumer path reaches it. CHANGELOG.md is documentation only. Not visible in this batch, so the next pass should check them: registry.SetMachineAutopilotDesiredMode and ListMachineAutopilot semantics, including whether flipping to live can affect provider routing or App Attest authorization (A-016, T-053/T-054); what fields MachineAutopilotStatus exposes (machine or serial identifiers, T-058); and whether admin mutations are audit-logged. The writeJSON and errorResponse helpers in package autopilot are defined in unchanged code. No concrete security regression found in the supplied diff.
